note: LocalASR catalog. Sizes reflect actual Hugging Face API data at build time; refined at runtime when online. released_year is a number (first weight release year), params_b is the parameter count in billions, quantization is the weight storage format.

engines.faster-whisper: CTranslate2: the fastest way to run Whisper models, int8 quantization, VAD, hotwords, batched decoding. The primary engine.
engines.whispercpp: whisper.cpp (GGML): minimal RAM, quantized q5_0/q8_0 models, a great choice for weak CPUs.
engines.vosk: Vosk (Kaldi): instant start, moderate RAM requirements, but no punctuation and noticeably less accurate than Whisper.
engines.qwen-asr: Qwen3-ASR (Alibaba) via transformers+torch: among the most accurate open ASR models, 30 languages, built-in punctuation. Requires torch (installed on demand).
engines.gigaam: GigaAM (Sber) via transformers+torch: best-in-class for Russian, punctuation and text normalization (e2e versions). Requires torch (installed on demand).

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo · Russian (int8, CT2)
models.languages_note: RU (priority) + 99 Whisper languages, best at Russian
models.description: A Russian fine-tune of Whisper Large v3 Turbo (809M). Author-reported AGG WER ≈ 9.4% — noticeably better than the base turbo on Russian speech: lectures, podcasts, live talks. CTranslate2 int8 build: 819 MB on disk, ~1.4 GB RAM, runs on both CPU and GPU. The best "Russian accuracy / size / speed" ratio.
models.recommended_for: The main choice for Russian lectures: accurate, fast, ~1.4 GB of memory

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo · Russian (int16, CT2)
models.description: The same Russian model in 16-bit precision: slightly more accurate on hard speech (noise, diction, terms) and twice as heavy. Pick it with 8+ GB RAM or a GPU with 4+ GB VRAM.
models.recommended_for: Maximum accuracy for Russian when memory allows

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo · Russian Code-Switch
models.description: A variant for lectures where Russian speech is heavily mixed with English terms ("deploy", "gradient descent", "backend"). Trades ~2% WER on pure Russian for never switching to English and never mangling terms.

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo · Russian (dvislobokov)
models.description: Another Russian fine-tune of the turbo model (base: openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo), already converted to CTranslate2. An alternative to coriollon — useful to run both on your recording and pick the better one.
models.recommended_for: A second Russian model for comparison

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo (multilingual, CT2)
models.languages_note: 99 languages; strong top ten: en, zh, de, fr, es, it, ja, ko, hi, pt + good ru
models.description: A distilled Whisper Large v3: 809M parameters instead of 1550M, 4 decoder layers — 6–8× faster than large-v3 at nearly the same accuracy. The universal choice when the language is unknown upfront or the recording is multilingual.
models.recommended_for: A universal fast option for any language

models.name: Whisper Large v3 (multilingual, CT2)
models.description: Maximum accuracy among Whisper models: 1550M parameters, 3.1 GB. Noticeably slower than turbo and more prone to silence hallucinations — LocalASR suppresses them (VAD + anti-repeats). Pick it when quality matters more than time and you have 6+ GB RAM / 5+ GB VRAM.
models.recommended_for: Maximum accuracy when time is not critical

models.name: Whisper Medium (multilingual, CT2)
models.description: 769M parameters. Inferior to the turbo models on Russian speech (it is the "classic" now) but noticeably faster than large-v3 on 8 GB RAM. A sensible compromise if the turbo models did not install.
models.recommended_for: A speed/quality compromise on 8 GB RAM

models.name: Distil Whisper Large v3 (English)
models.description: A distilled English-only model: within 1.5% WER of large-v3 at 6× the speed. NOT suitable for Russian lectures — enable it only for transcribing English talks.

models.name: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (transformer, SOTA 2026)
models.description: The flagship of open ASR: a Whisper-type audio encoder + the Qwen3 language model. Beats open Whisper builds on benchmarks and competes with commercial APIs. Punctuation and clean text out of the box, robust to noise and music, understands language switching. Requires torch and 10+ GB RAM (or a GPU with 6+ GB VRAM).
models.recommended_for: Maximum accuracy in any language when the hardware allows

models.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (transformer, fast)
models.description: The junior model of the Qwen3-ASR family: a balance of accuracy and speed, noticeably stronger than Whisper-medium on Russian and comparable to turbo builds at a smaller size. A good choice when you want the "new generation" but lack 10 GB RAM for the 1.7B.
models.recommended_for: Modern accuracy with moderate requirements (4–8 GB RAM)

models.name: GigaAM v3 E2E RNNT (Sber, Russian, with punctuation)
models.languages_note: Russian only, but best-in-class: punctuation and text normalization
models.description: Sber's Russian conformer model (220M): 30% more accurate than its predecessors on new domains (call centers, voice messages, music), wins 70:30 head-to-head against Whisper-large-v3. The e2e version delivers punctuation and normalized text right away. Only 449 MB — SOTA Russian for weak hardware. Requires torch.
models.recommended_for: The best Russian text on modest hardware: 449 MB, built-in punctuation

models.name: GigaAM v3 E2E CTC (Sber, Russian, fast)
models.languages_note: Russian only; punctuation and text normalization
models.description: The same GigaAM v3 Russian base but with a CTC decoder: faster than the RNNT version, accuracy a few tenths of a percent lower. Choose it when the speed of processing a large lecture folder matters more.
models.recommended_for: Fast Russian with punctuation on weak hardware

models.name: GigaAM Multilingual CTC (Sber, 70+ languages)
models.languages_note: 70+ languages; strongest at ru, kk, ky, uz; average English
models.description: The GigaAM multilingual line (220M encoder, pretrained on 2M hours, 70+ languages): best-in-class WER for Russian, Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Uzbek. No punctuation (CTC decodes per character). Handy for CIS-language recordings that Whisper knows worse.
models.recommended_for: Russian + CIS languages (kk, ky, uz) when punctuation is not required

models.name: GigaAM Multilingual Large CTC (Sber, 600M)
models.languages_note: 70+ languages; maximum accuracy of the Multilingual line
models.description: The senior encoder (600M) of the GigaAM multilingual line: the family's best accuracy for Russian and CIS languages at twice the size and memory. No punctuation.
models.recommended_for: Maximum accuracy for Russian/CIS without Whisper

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo q5_0 (whisper.cpp)
models.description: A quantized q5_0 turbo model for whisper.cpp: 574 MB on disk and ~900 MB RAM at accuracy close to full turbo. The best "big model on weak hardware" option: runs on CPU and can use the GPU (if pywhispercpp is built with CUDA).
models.recommended_for: Accurate transcription on 4–8 GB RAM without a GPU

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo (whisper.cpp)
models.description: The full (non-quantized) turbo model in GGML format. A few tenths of a percent more accurate than q5_0 but three times heavier on memory.

models.name: Whisper Large v3 q5_0 (whisper.cpp)
models.description: The quantized full large-v3: 1.1 GB instead of 2.9 GB. Slower than turbo (32 decoder layers) but maximum language coverage among the "lightweight" options.

models.name: Whisper Medium (whisper.cpp)
models.description: The medium model in GGML. Makes sense only if faster-whisper does not work on your hardware for some reason.

models.name: Vosk Russian 0.42 (Kaldi)
models.description: The large Russian Kaldi model. WER ≈ 4.5% on audiobooks and 11–20% on live speech (YouTube/calls) — much weaker than Whisper on noisy lectures. But it transcribes faster than realtime even on an old CPU and needs no GPU. No punctuation or capitals (LocalASR adds the minimum).
models.recommended_for: Weak CPU without a GPU: faster than realtime at all costs
